newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to issue 100 bln baht zero coupon bond.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to issue 100 bln baht zero coupon bond.

text.p: A senior Thai central bank official said on Saturday Thailand would issue 100 billion baht zero coupon bonds in two tranches in the near future.
The bonds will be issued in two 50 billion baht tranches, assistant central bank governor Siri Ganjarerndee told reporters.
Funds from the bond issues will be used to buy substandard assets and non-performing loans from finance companies and banks at up to 50 percent of their market valuation, Siri said.
The bonds will have a maturity of seven years, Central Bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond told reporters.
"The whole idea of issuing zero coupon bonds is basically to help ease problems of non-performing loans faced by finance companies," he said.
The Bank of Thailand plans to form an entity funded by the bonds which will buy the assets from troubled firms, he said.
The central bank was still finalising details but would likely seek cabinet approval for the measures on Tuesday, Rerngchai said.
Thai finance companies, hit by a slump in the Thai property sector and a slowing economy, are facing a liquidity crunch.
In an unprecedented move last Monday the central bank suspended share trading on all bank and finance stocks as it moved to shore up the sector.
It then identified 10 struggling firms and ordered them to increase their capital.
The bond-based rescue and buyout of poor quality loans from finance companies was a solution based on U.S. and Swedish models which would not burden state funds, Rerngchai said.
